sanskrit: na sadyo 'rīn vinirhanyād dṛṣṭasya vijayo 'jvaraḥ na yaḥ śalyaṃ ghaṭṭayati navaṃ ca kurute vraṇam
english: Let him not strike down his foes in haste; the victory of the watchful comes without fever. He who does not jar the embedded barb, nor opens up a fresh wound, prospers.

sanskrit: prāpte ca praharet kāle na sa saṃvartate punaḥ hantukāmasya devendra puruṣasya ripuṃ prati
english: But when the appointed time has come, let him strike; for the moment does not return again to the man who longs, O lord of the gods, to slay his enemy.

sanskrit: yaḥ kālo hi vyatikrāmet puruṣaṃ kālakāṅkṣiṇam durlabhaḥ sa punaḥ kālaḥ kāladharmacikīrṣuṇā
english: For the occasion that slips past the man who awaits his occasion is hard for him to regain, though he would act in accord with the law of timeliness.

sanskrit: aurjasthyaṃ vijayed evaṃ saṃgṛhṇan sādhusaṃmatān kālena sādhayen nityaṃ nāprāpte 'bhinipīḍayet
english: Thus let him master his own vigor, winning over the men whom the good esteem; let him always accomplish his ends in their season, and not press hard before the time has come.

sanskrit: vihāya kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca tathāhaṃkāram eva ca yukto vivaram anvicched ahitānāṃ puraṃdara
english: Setting aside desire and wrath, and pride as well, the disciplined king should watch for the opening in his foes, O Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: mārdavaṃ daṇḍa ālasyaṃ pramādaś ca surottama māyāś ca vividhāḥ śakra sādhayanty avicakṣaṇam
english: Softness, harshness, sloth, and heedlessness, O best of gods, and manifold deceits, O Śakra — these overcome the man who lacks discernment.

sanskrit: nihatyaitāni catvāri māyāṃ pratividhāya ca tataḥ śaknoti śatrūṇāṃ prahartum avicārayan
english: Having destroyed these four, and having warded off deceit, he is then able to strike his enemies without hesitation.

sanskrit: yadaivaikena śakyeta guhyaṃ kartuṃ tadācaret yacchanti sacivā guhyaṃ mitho vidrāvayanty api
english: Whenever a secret design can be carried out by one alone, let him do it so; for ministers let secrets slip among themselves, and even betray them.

sanskrit: aśakyam iti kṛtvā vā tato 'nyaiḥ saṃvidaṃ caret brahmadaṇḍam adṛṣṭeṣu dṛṣṭeṣu caturaṅgiṇīm
english: Or, judging a thing beyond his single power, let him then make common counsel with others — the rod of brahman against unseen foes, the fourfold army against those in sight.

sanskrit: bhedaṃ ca prathamaṃ yuñjyāt tūṣṇīṃdaṇḍaṃ tathaiva ca kāle prayojayed rājā tasmiṃs tasmiṃs tadā tadā
english: Let him first employ division, and likewise silent chastisement; the king should apply each of these in its proper season, this one now and that one then.

sanskrit: praṇipātaṃ ca gaccheta kāle śatror balīyasaḥ yukto 'sya vadham anvicched apramattaḥ pramādyataḥ
english: And he should bow in submission, in due season, before an enemy stronger than himself; yet, disciplined and unheedful of nothing, let him seek that foe's destruction when the foe grows careless.

sanskrit: praṇipātena dānena vācā madhurayā bruvan amitram upaseveta na tu jātu viśaṅkayet
english: With homage, with gifts, and speaking in honeyed words, let him attend upon his enemy, yet never let the enemy grow suspicious of him.

sanskrit: sthānāni śaṅkitānāṃ ca nityam eva vivarjayet na ca teṣv āśvased drugdhvā jāgratīha nirākṛtāḥ
english: Let him ever shun the haunts of men who are wary of him, and place no trust in them; for once injured, those who have been spurned remain watchful here.

sanskrit: na hy ato duṣkaraṃ karma kiṃ cid asti surottama yathā vividhavṛttānām aiśvaryam amarādhipa
english: For there is no task harder than this, O best of gods, than to hold sovereignty over men of manifold conduct, O lord of the immortals.

sanskrit: tathā vividhaśīlānām api saṃbhava ucyate yateta yogam āsthāya mitrāmitrān avārayan
english: So too is it called the very nature of men of varied dispositions. Let him strive, taking his stand upon strategy, holding off both friend and foe.

sanskrit: mṛdum apy avamanyante tīkṣṇād udvijate janaḥ mātīkṣṇo māmṛdur bhūs tvaṃ tīkṣṇo bhava mṛdur bhava
english: The gentle man they despise, yet from the harsh the people shrink. Be neither too harsh nor too gentle: be harsh, be gentle, each in its turn.

sanskrit: yathā vapre vegavati sarvataḥsaṃplutodake nityaṃ vivaraṇād bādhas tathā rājyaṃ pramādyataḥ
english: As an embankment, when the rushing waters flood it on every side, is breached forever once a gap appears, so is the kingdom of the heedless king.

sanskrit: na banūn abhiyuñjīta yaugapadyena śātravān sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍena ca puraṃdara
english: Let him not assail many foes at once, O Puraṃdara, but by conciliation, by gift, by division, and by force.

sanskrit: ekaikam eṣāṃ niṣpiṃṣañ śiṣṭeṣu nipuṇaṃ caret na ca śakto 'pi medhāvī sarvān evārabhen nṛpaḥ
english: Crushing them one by one, let him deal skillfully with those that remain; for even when able, the wise king should not take on all of them together.

sanskrit: yadā syān mahatī senā hayanāgarathākulā padātiyantrabahulā svanuraktā ṣaḍaṅginī
english: When his army is great, thronged with horses, elephants, and chariots, abounding in foot soldiers and engines of war, well-affectioned and complete in its six divisions —

sanskrit: yadā bahuvidhāṃ vṛddhiṃ manyate pratilomataḥ tadā vivṛtya prahared dasyūnām avicārayan
english: and when he reckons his manifold increase against the adverse measure of his foes, then let him strike openly at the marauders, without hesitation.

sanskrit: na sāma daṇḍopaniṣat praśasyate; na mārdavaṃ śatruṣu yātrikaṃ sadā na sasyaghāto na ca saṃkarakriyā; na cāpi bhūyaḥ prakṛter vicāraṇā
english: Conciliation that ends in the rod is not commended, nor is gentleness ever a fit policy of campaign toward enemies; neither the destruction of crops, nor the breeding of confusion, nor again any wavering from one's settled nature.

sanskrit: māyāvibhedānupasarjanāni; pāpaṃ tathaiva spaśasaṃprayogāt āptair manuṣyair upacārayeta; pureṣu rāṣṭreṣu ca saṃprayuktaḥ
english: Deceits, divisions, and the planting of dissension, and likewise the working of harm through the deployment of spies — these let him carry out through trusted men, engaged in the cities and the realms of his foes.

sanskrit: purāṇi caiṣām anusṛtya bhūmipāḥ; pureṣu bhogān nikhilān ihājayan pureṣu nītiṃ vihitāṃ yathāvidhi; prayojayanto balavṛtrasūdana
english: Pursuing the cities of these foes, the lords of earth win for themselves all the enjoyments those cities hold, applying in them the policy ordained according to rule, O slayer of Bala and Vṛtra.

sanskrit: pradāya gūḍhāni vasūni nāma; pracchidya bhogān avadhāya ca svān duṣṭāḥ svadoṣair iti kīrtayitvā; pureṣu rāṣṭreṣu ca yojayanti
english: Having bestowed hidden wealth in the name of others, having cut off the foe's enjoyments and secured their own, and having proclaimed the wicked condemned by their own faults, they set their men to work in those cities and realms.

sanskrit: tathaiva cānyai ratiśāstravedibhiḥ; svalaṃkṛtaiḥ śāstravidhānadṛṣṭibhiḥ suśikṣitair bhāṣyakathāviśāradaiḥ; pareṣu kṛtyān upadhārayasva
english: And likewise, through others well versed in the arts of pleasure, finely adorned, schooled in the prescriptions of the treatises, well-trained, and skilled in discourse and tale — through these, mark well, he sets afoot his designs among his foes.

sanskrit: indra uvāca kāni liṅgāni duṣṭasya bhavanti dvijasattama kathaṃ duṣṭaṃ vijānīyād etat pṛṣṭo bravīhi me
english: Indra said: What are the marks of a corrupted man, O best of the twice-born? How may one know the corrupt? Asked this, declare it to me.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca parokṣam aguṇān āha sadguṇān abhyasūyati parair vā kīrtyamāneṣu tūṣṇīm āste parāṅmukhaḥ
english: Bṛhaspati said: Behind one's back he speaks of one's faults, and at one's true virtues he carps; or when others are praised, he sits silent, his face turned away.

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃbhāve 'pi hi jñānaṃ na ced bhavati kāraṇam viśvāsam oṣṭhasaṃdaṃśaṃ śirasaś ca prakampanam
english: Even in his silence may his mind be read, if there be no other cause for it — by his feigned trust, the biting of his lip, and the trembling of his head.

sanskrit: karoty abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃsṛṣṭam asaṃsṛṣṭaś ca bhāṣate adṛṣṭito vikurute dṛṣṭvā vā nābhibhāṣate
english: He keeps drawing close again and again, then speaks while keeping his distance; out of sight he works against you, and, having seen you, does not address you.

sanskrit: pṛthag etya samaśnāti nedam adya yathāvidhi āsane śayane yāne bhāvā lakṣyā viśeṣataḥ
english: He comes apart from the rest and eats alone — "this fare today is not as it should be" — his true feelings to be discerned, above all, in his sitting, his lying down, and his going about.

sanskrit: ārtir ārte priye prītir etāvan mitralakṣaṇam viparītaṃ tu boddhavyam arilakṣaṇam eva tat
english: Distress at a friend's distress, joy at his joy — only this is the mark of a friend; but the contrary is to be understood as the very mark of an enemy.

sanskrit: etāny evaṃ yathoktāni budhyethās tridaśādhipa puruṣāṇāṃ praduṣṭānāṃ svabhāvo balavattaraḥ
english: These signs, declared just as I have told them, you should mark, O lord of the thirty gods; in corrupted men the inborn nature proves the stronger force.

sanskrit: iti duṣṭasya vijñānam uktaṃ te surasattama niśāmya śāstratattvārthaṃ yathāvad amareśvara
english: Thus the discernment of the corrupt has been told to you, O best of gods, having grasped the true meaning of the treatise as it is, O lord of the immortals.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa tad vacaḥ śatrunibarhaṇe ratas; tathā cakārāvitathaṃ bṛhaspateḥ cacāra kāle vijayāya cārihā; vaśaṃ ca śatrūn anayat puraṃdaraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Bent upon the destruction of his foes, he made the word of Bṛhaspati come true; and Puraṃdara, slayer of enemies, acted in due season for victory and brought his foes beneath his sway.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhārmiko 'rthān asaṃprāpya rājāmātyaiḥ prabādhitaḥ cyutaḥ kośāc ca daṇḍāc ca sukham icchan kathaṃ caret
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A righteous king who has failed to win wealth, oppressed by hostile ministers, fallen from his treasury and from his power of chastisement — how should he conduct himself if he seeks his welfare?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāyaṃ kṣemadarśīyam itihāso 'nugīyate tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point an old tale is sung, the dialogue of Kṣemadarśin. I shall set it forth to you; mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: kṣemadarśaṃ nṛpasutaṃ yatra kṣīṇabalaṃ purā muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīya ājagāmeti naḥ śrutam taṃ papracchopasaṃgṛhya kṛcchrām āpadam āsthitaḥ
english: To the prince Kṣemadarśin, whose strength was spent, the sage Kālakavṛkṣīya once came of old — so we have heard. Caught in dire distress, the prince clasped his feet and questioned him.

sanskrit: artheṣu bhāgī puruṣa īhamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ alabdhvā madvidho rājyaṃ brahman kiṃ kartum arhati
english: A man who is heir to wealth, striving for it again and again, yet failing to win the kingdom — what, O brāhmaṇa, ought one like me to do?

sanskrit: anyatra maraṇāt steyād anyatra parasaṃśrayāt kṣudrād anyatra cācārāt tan mamācakṣva sattama
english: Apart from death, apart from theft, apart from dependence on another, apart from base conduct — declare that to me, O most excellent one.

sanskrit: vyādhinā cābhipannasya mānasenetareṇa vā bahuśrutaḥ kṛtaprajñas tvadvidhaḥ śaraṇaṃ bhavet
english: For one afflicted by sickness, whether of the mind or of the other kind, a man of wide learning and ripened wisdom such as you becomes a refuge.

sanskrit: nirvidya hi naraḥ kāmān niyamya sukham edhate tyaktvā prītiṃ ca śokaṃ ca labdhvāprītimayaṃ vasu
english: For a man, growing weary of desires and restraining them, increases in happiness, having let go both delight and grief, and gained a wealth that lies beyond pleasure.

sanskrit: sukham arthāśrayaṃ yeṣām anuśocāmi tān aham mama hy arthāḥ subahavo naṣṭāḥ svapna ivāgatāḥ
english: Those whose happiness rests upon riches — for them I grieve; for my own riches, very many, have perished, having come like a dream.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ bata kurvanti mahato 'rthāṃs tyajanti ye vayaṃ tv enān parityaktum asato 'pi na śaknumaḥ
english: A hard thing indeed do they accomplish, those who renounce great riches; yet we cannot bring ourselves to relinquish them, unreal though they be.

sanskrit: imām avasthāṃ saṃprāptaṃ dīnam ārtaṃ śriyaś cyutam yad anyat sukham astīha tad brahmann anuśādhi mām
english: Fallen into this plight, wretched, stricken, cast down from fortune — whatever other happiness there is here, instruct me in that, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kausalyenaivam uktas tu rājaputreṇa dhīmatā muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīyaḥ pratyuvāca mahādyutiḥ
english: Thus addressed by the wise prince of Kosala, the sage Kālakavṛkṣīya, of great radiance, replied:

sanskrit: purastād eva te buddhir iyaṃ kāryā vijānataḥ anityaṃ sarvam evedam ahaṃ ca mama cāsti yat
english: This understanding should have been yours from the very first, since you are a man of discernment: that all this is impermanent — both "I" and whatever is "mine."

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cin manyase 'stīti sarvaṃ nāstīti viddhi tat evaṃ na vyathate prājñaḥ kṛcchrām apy āpadaṃ gataḥ
english: Whatever you suppose to be — know that all of it is not. So the wise man is not shaken, even when fallen into dire distress.

sanskrit: yad dhi bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca dhruvaṃ tan na bhaviṣyati evaṃ viditavedyas tvam adharmebhyaḥ pramokṣyase
english: For what has come to be, and what is yet to be, will surely cease to be. Knowing thus what is to be known, you shall be freed from unrighteous deeds.

sanskrit: yac ca pūrve samāhāre yac ca pūrvatare pare sarvaṃ tan nāsti tac caiva taj jñātvā ko 'nusaṃjvaret
english: What was in the former gathering of things, and what was in the gathering still earlier — all that is gone, just gone. Knowing this, who would burn with sorrow?

sanskrit: bhūtvā ca na bhavaty etad abhūtvā ca bhavaty api śoke na hy asti sāmarthyaṃ śokaṃ kuryāt kathaṃ naraḥ
english: This world, having been, ceases to be, and, not having been, comes to be again. In grief there lies no power to mend; how then should a man give way to grief?

sanskrit: kva nu te 'dya pitā rājan kva nu te 'dya pitāmahaḥ na tvaṃ paśyasi tān adya na tvā paśyanti te 'pi ca
english: Where now, O king, is your father today? Where now today your grandsire? You do not see them now, nor do they any longer see you.

sanskrit: ātmano 'dhruvatāṃ paśyaṃs tāṃs tvaṃ kim anuśocasi buddhyā caivānubudhyasva dhruvaṃ hi na bhaviṣyasi
english: Seeing your own impermanence, why do you mourn for them? And awaken by your understanding to this: that you too will surely cease to be.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca nṛpate śatravaḥ suhṛdaś ca te avaśyaṃ na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarvaṃ ca na bhaviṣyati
english: I and you, O king, your enemies and your friends — inevitably we shall cease to be, and all things shall cease to be.

sanskrit: ye tu viṃśativarṣā vai triṃśadvarṣāś ca mānavāḥ arvāg eva hi te sarve mariṣyanti śaracchatāt
english: Those men who are twenty years of age, and those who are thirty — all of them, indeed, will die well short of a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: api cen mahato vittād vipramucyeta pūruṣaḥ naitan mameti tan matvā kurvīta priyam ātmanaḥ
english: And even if a man be parted from great wealth, let him, thinking "this is not mine," do what is good for his own soul.

sanskrit: anāgataṃ yan na mameti vidyād; atikrāntaṃ yan na mameti vidyāt diṣṭaṃ balīya iti manyamānās; te paṇḍitās tat satāṃ sthānam āhuḥ
english: What has not yet come, let him know is not his; what has passed away, let him know is not his. Holding that destiny is the stronger — such men are the wise, and that, they say, is the station of the good.

sanskrit: anāḍhyāś cāpi jīvanti rājyaṃ cāpy anuśāsate buddhipauruṣasaṃpannās tvayā tulyādhikā janāḥ
english: Even men without riches live, and even rule a kingdom — men endowed with wisdom and manliness, your equals and your betters.

sanskrit: na ca tvam iva śocanti tasmāt tvam api mā śucaḥ kiṃ nu tvaṃ tair na vai śreyāṃs tulyo vā buddhipauruṣaiḥ
english: And they do not grieve as you do; therefore do not you grieve either. Are you not their better, or at least their equal, in wisdom and in manliness?

sanskrit: rājaputra uvāca yādṛcchikaṃ mamāsīt tad rājyam ity eva cintaye hriyate sarvam evedaṃ kālena mahatā dvija
english: The prince said: That kingdom of mine came to me by mere chance — so I reckon it; and all this, O brāhmaṇa, is being borne away by mighty Time.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ hriyamāṇasya srotaseva tapodhana phalam etat prapaśyāmi yathālabdhena vartaye
english: As it is thus swept away, as if by a current, O you whose wealth is austerity, this fruit of it I clearly see: that I must live by what comes to me.

sanskrit: munir uvāca anāgatam atītaṃ ca yathā tathyaviniścayāt nānuśocasi kausalya sarvārtheṣu tathā bhava
english: The sage said: Since, by a true settling of the matter, you do not grieve for the future or the past, O prince of Kosala, be so in all your concerns.

sanskrit: avāpyān kāmayasvārthān nānavāpyān kadā cana pratyutpannān anubhavan mā śucas tvam anāgatān
english: Desire only the ends that may be attained, never those that cannot; experiencing the things that are present, do not grieve for those not yet come.

sanskrit: yathā labdhopapannārthas tathā kausalya raṃsyase kaccic chuddhasvabhāvena śriyā hīno na śocasi
english: As one furnished with the wealth that has come to you, so will you, O prince of Kosala, take your delight. Surely, with a nature made pure, you do not grieve though bereft of fortune?

sanskrit: purastād bhūtapūrvatvād dhīnabhāgyo hi durmatiḥ dhātāraṃ garhate nityaṃ labdhārthāṃś ca na mṛṣyate
english: For the ill-minded man of meager fortune, because of what he once possessed before, forever blames the Ordainer, and cannot endure those who have won wealth.

sanskrit: anarhān api caivānyān manyate śrīmato janān etasmāt kāraṇād etad duḥkhaṃ bhūyo 'nuvartate
english: And he deems even other, unworthy folk to be men of fortune; for this very reason this suffering of his pursues him all the more.

sanskrit: īrṣyāticchedasaṃpannā rājan puruṣamāninaḥ kaccit tvaṃ na tathā prājña matsarī kosalādhipa
english: Men full of envy and overreaching, O king, who pride themselves on their manhood — surely you, O wise lord of Kosala, are not thus, not given to spite?

sanskrit: sahasva śriyam anyeṣāṃ yady api tvayi nāsti sā anyatrāpi satīṃ lakṣmīṃ kuśalā bhuñjate janāḥ abhiviṣyandate śrīr hi saty api dviṣato janāt
english: Bear with the fortune of others, even though it be not yours; able men enjoy the prosperity that abides elsewhere as well. For fortune overflows abundantly, even where there is one who hates.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ ca putrapautraṃ ca manuṣyā dharmacāriṇaḥ tyāgadharmavido vīrāḥ svayam eva tyajanty uta
english: Fortune too, and sons and grandsons, men of righteous walk — heroes who know the law of renunciation — give up of their own accord.

sanskrit: bahu saṃkasukaṃ dṛṣṭvā vivitsāsādhanena ca tathānye saṃtyajanty enaṃ matvā paramadurlabham
english: Seeing how unsteady and troublesome it is, and by the means of seeking knowledge, still others renounce this fortune, judging the higher good most hard to win.

sanskrit: tvaṃ punaḥ prājñarūpaḥ san kṛpaṇaṃ paritapyase akāmyān kāmayāno 'rthān parācīnān upadrutān
english: You, on the other hand, though you wear the form of a wise man, torment yourself most pitiably, longing for ends not to be longed for — gains turned away from you and beset with troubles.

sanskrit: tāṃ buddhim upajijñāsus tvam evainān parityaja anarthāṃś cārtharūpeṇa arthāṃś cānartharūpataḥ
english: Seeking to know that higher wisdom, do you yourself abandon them — those misfortunes that wear the shape of gain, and those gains that wear the shape of misfortune.

sanskrit: arthāyaiva hi keṣāṃ cid dhananāśo bhavaty uta anantyaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ matvā śriyam anyaḥ parīkṣate
english: For some, indeed, the loss of wealth itself turns to gain; deeming that happiness to be without end, one looks askance at fortune.

sanskrit: ramamāṇaḥ śriyā kaś cin nānyac chreyo 'bhimanyate tathā tasyehamānasya samārambho vinaśyati
english: Some man, taking delight in fortune, esteems no other good above it; and so, as he strives, his very undertaking comes to ruin.

sanskrit: kṛcchrāl labdham abhipretaṃ yadā kausalya naśyati tadā nirvidyate so 'rthāt paribhagnakramo naraḥ
english: When what was longed for and won with toil is lost, O prince of Kosala, then that man, his ordered course shattered, grows wearied of wealth.

sanskrit: dharmam eke 'bhipadyante kalyāṇābhijanā narāḥ paratra sukham icchanto nirvidyeyuś ca laukikāt
english: Some men, born of noble stock, betake themselves to righteousness, desiring happiness in the world beyond, and grow weary of worldly things.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ saṃtyajanty eke dhanalobhaparā narāḥ na jīvitārthaṃ manyante puruṣā hi dhanād ṛte
english: Some men, given over to greed for wealth, cast away their very lives; for such men hold life itself worth nothing apart from riches.

sanskrit: paśya teṣāṃ kṛpaṇatāṃ paśya teṣām abuddhitām adhruve jīvite mohād arthatṛṣṇām upāśritāḥ
english: Behold their wretchedness, behold their want of understanding — who, in this uncertain life, out of delusion cling to the thirst for wealth.

sanskrit: saṃcaye ca vināśānte maraṇānte ca jīvite saṃyoge viprayogānte ko nu vipraṇayen manaḥ
english: When hoarding ends in loss, and life ends in death, and union ends in parting — who, then, would set his heart upon them?

sanskrit: dhanaṃ vā puruṣaṃ rājan puruṣo vā punar dhanam avaśyaṃ prajahāty etat tad vidvān ko 'nusaṃjvaret
english: Either wealth forsakes the man, O king, or the man in turn forsakes his wealth; inevitably the one parts from the other. Knowing this, what wise man would burn with sorrow?
